pains.title: Short visits look profitable, but admin time hides the margin
pains.problem: Short medication visits carry unpaid work like prior authorizations and refill requests. A blended report hides whether medication, therapy, TMS or Spravato earns the money.
pains.how: Lucid splits your books by service line and provider and reports margin for each one every month. Your biller keeps running billing.

pains.title: TMS devices: buy, lease or pay per session
pains.problem: The device is a large up front choice. Buying, leasing or paying per session changes your cash needs, cost per session and the timing of the tax deduction.
pains.how: Lucid models sessions, reimbursement and financing to show your break even volume. Your CPA plans Section 179 or bonus depreciation against year end income. Lucid does not arrange financing.

pains.title: Spravato and ketamine: cash out before cash in
pains.problem: Spravato is bought and billed, so you pay for each dose before payment arrives. A denial after the dose is given is a direct loss.
pains.how: Lucid's cash flow forecast counts the drug outlay before payment lands, with payer mix tracking. Prepaid packages are held as deposits until sessions are delivered. Your biller handles claims and denials.

faq.q: Should my psychiatric nurse practitioners be 1099 or W-2?
faq.a: It depends on how much control you have over their schedule, patients and records, not on what the paperwork says. Lucid's classification review looks at how each prescriber really works and shows the cost of each option, including payroll tax and benefits. Your attorney confirms the legal side, including any collaboration agreement.

faq.q: How much money is my psychiatry practice losing to no-shows?
faq.a: No shows cost you the visit and often the fixed staff time, and long visits and device sessions lose the most. Lucid's reporting shows revenue and margin by provider, so you can judge fees or overbooking with real numbers.

faq.q: Should my psychiatry practice go cash-pay or stay in network?
faq.a: It comes down to what you really net per hour from each payer after billing cost, denials and no-shows. Lucid builds that comparison from your own books and models a few scenarios. Many groups end up with a mix, and you see the numbers before changing anything.

faq.q: How do I know if my psychiatry practice is collecting all it should?
faq.a: Lucid compares what you billed with what you actually collected, by payer and provider, and reports receivable aging so you see how old the unpaid balances are. If money is slipping, you see where, and your biller can focus on the oldest and largest items.

faq.q: Is adding another state to my telepsychiatry practice worth the cost?
faq.a: Lucid's CFO scenario planning can model a new state against its license, renewal, malpractice and admin costs, and Lucid handles multi state filings. Licensing and legal questions go to your counsel or board.
